neighborhoods.name: National Mall and downtown
neighborhoods.tip: Museums and memorials are close together but the Mall is long: about 2 miles from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial. Metro stations: Smithsonian, Federal Triangle, L'Enfant Plaza.

neighborhoods.name: Penn Quarter and Chinatown
neighborhoods.tip: Central and lively at night, a few minutes' walk to the museums. Gallery Place and Archives stations.

neighborhoods.name: Capitol Hill
neighborhoods.tip: Rowhouse streets behind the Capitol, with Eastern Market. Capitol South, Eastern Market and Union Station stations.

neighborhoods.name: NoMa and Union Market
neighborhoods.tip: Newer apartments and hotels near Union Station and the Union Market food hall. NoMa-Gallaudet station.

neighborhoods.name: Foggy Bottom and the West End
neighborhoods.tip: Near the Lincoln Memorial, the river and Georgetown. Foggy Bottom station is the closest Metro to Georgetown.

neighborhoods.name: Georgetown
neighborhoods.tip: Brick Federal houses, shops and the canal. No Metro stop: walk from Foggy Bottom, or take a bus or ride.

neighborhoods.name: Dupont Circle and Logan Circle
neighborhoods.tip: Cafes, embassies and Victorian rowhouses, about 30 minutes' walk or a short Metro ride to the Mall. Dupont Circle station.

neighborhoods.name: U Street, Shaw and Adams Morgan
neighborhoods.tip: Music, nightlife and restaurants. U Street and Shaw stations.

neighborhoods.name: The Wharf and Navy Yard
neighborhoods.tip: Waterfront promenade, restaurants and the fish market. Waterfront and Navy Yard stations.

neighborhoods.name: Arlington, Virginia
neighborhoods.tip: Across the Potomac with direct Metro lines into DC: Rosslyn, Pentagon City, Crystal City.

neighborhoods.name: Old Town Alexandria, Virginia
neighborhoods.tip: Historic brick town on the river, about 20 minutes by Metro from downtown DC. King Street-Old Town station.

neighborhoods.name: Maryland suburbs (Bethesda, Silver Spring…)
neighborhoods.tip: Red Line Metro runs into the city from Bethesda and Silver Spring.

airports.name: Reagan National airport (DCA)
airports.tip: The closest airport, in Virginia. Metro Blue and Yellow lines from the terminals; taxis are metered and take cash or card.

airports.name: Dulles airport (IAD)
airports.tip: Most long-haul flights land here, in Virginia. The Silver Line takes about 50 minutes to Metro Center; by road it can take much longer at rush hour.

airports.name: Baltimore airport (BWI)
airports.tip: In Maryland. A free 24-hour shuttle goes to the BWI rail station; MARC or Amtrak trains reach Union Station in about 35 minutes.

items.title: Metro: just tap your card or phone
items.text: Tap a contactless credit or debit card, or your phone or watch, at the faregate, and tap out with the same one. Each rider needs their own card or phone. No need to buy a SmarTrip card.

items.title: Metro fares
items.text: Weekdays $2.25 to $6.75 depending on distance. After 9:30 p.m. on weeknights and all weekend, $2.25 to $2.50. Buses are $2.25, paid the same way.

items.title: From the airports
items.text: Reagan National: Blue or Yellow Line from the terminal. Dulles: Silver Line, about 50 minutes to Metro Center. BWI: free shuttle to the rail station, then MARC or Amtrak to Union Station (about 35 minutes).

items.title: Taxis and ride apps
items.text: DC taxis use the meter; you can hail one on the street or find one at hotels and Union Station. Uber and Lyft work across DC, Virginia and Maryland, including the airports.

items.title: Walking the Mall
items.text: The Mall is about 2 miles long, Capitol to Lincoln Memorial. The museums sit in the middle; the memorials are at the west end, around the Reflecting Pool and the Tidal Basin. Wear comfortable shoes and plan rests.

items.title: Driving and parking
items.text: Parking downtown is scarce and costly, and the Smithsonian museums on the Mall have no parking. Use Metro or a ride app in the city; a car only helps for Mount Vernon or the Udvar-Hazy Center.

getting_around.source: WMATA (Tap. Ride. Go. and 2024 fare tables, fares unchanged for FY2027), BWI and Mount Vernon official sites, Smithsonian, Reagan National taxi page

taxis.intro_bold: DC taxis run on the meter.
taxis.intro: Hail one on the street or find one at hotels, Union Station and the airports. At Reagan National, taxis wait outside baggage claim and take cash or card. Tip about 15 to 20%.
taxis.apps: Uber and Lyft work across DC, Virginia and Maryland. Check the price in the app before you book.

periods.label: all times
periods.rule: all times, incl. $0.50 surcharge and $1 fuel surcharge

taxi_tariff.rush_note: The meter adds $25 an hour when the taxi is stopped or crawling, so traffic costs more. Trips from Reagan National and Dulles start in Virginia and use the airport's own taxi rates; airport fees and tolls are added.
taxi_tariff.note: Rough estimate from the DC meter rates ($4.00 start, $2.56 a mile, shown here per km) and straight-line distance. The meter decides. The $1 fuel surcharge runs until Dec 25, 2026.
taxi_tariff.source: DC Department of For-Hire Vehicles taxicab fares (in force since Aug 2, 2024)

rides.title: Drivers and rides
rides.intro: In the city, Metro, taxis and ride apps cover almost everything. For Mount Vernon or a day in Virginia, a ride app or a car is simplest.

items.name: Taxis at Reagan National
items.what: Metered taxis wait outside baggage claim at each terminal and take cash or card.

items.name: Uber and Lyft
items.what: Ride apps work across the region, including the three airports.

rides.note: Listed because an official source names them, not because Wanderings has ridden with them.
